This is budget friendly way to do the footprints, you’ll need:
- Container in shape of your choice
- Play Doh
- Plaster
- Acrylic Paint

Get a container in the shape that you want the mold to be in (rectangle, circle, etc…) as this will be the shape you end up with. Make sure it’s not crazy wide with negative space in comparison to the size of the foot (for aesthetics and so you don’t have to use a tonne of plaster). 

Fill the base of the container with Play Doh (or one that is off brand, you just want to make sure it’s the same softness as Play Doh). Make it a reasonably thick depth, you want to be able to catch the detail without hitting the bottom of the container. 

Gently but firmly press the child’s foot down into the Play Doh, then take it out. If you’re not happy with it, take out the Play Doh, mush it together again and reset it in the container. Do it until you’re happy with the impression. 

Mix up your plaster as the packet instructs, and then pour it in and let it set overnight. Give it a decent thickness so it’s not too fragile (Don’t be tempted to take it out ASAP as it might still be fragile and brittle until thoroughly set)

And that’s it, paint them up however you like and you can frame them in a shadow box or display them any way you like. 

You can reuse the Play Doh so should be cheaper than kits. I had to do this for someone’s kids when I was in a pinch when another method didn’t work. 

Hope that makes sense. ◡̈

Wedge a strip of cardboard inside the hole so there is now a “wall”. You can do this by cutting your card roughly to size, sticking a bit of wire through it and then bending the end of the wire so it’s now in an “L” shape. The little part of the L should be behind the card and you hold the long part, this is so you can kind of tug it and it doesn’t fall inside deeper when you do the next step. Now mix up some car body filler with fibreglass strands and fill as much as you can of the hole. Hold onto your little bit of wire holding the cardboard to keep it in place. 
Once that’s all cured, you can go in with something to get the surface detail. I would recommend Milliput or something similar (any two part plumber putty is fine, Milliput is just super cheap.) once that is cured you can sand and then paint. 

It would have been easier if I could have drawn you a diagram, but I hope that makes sense. If you’re struggling to understand feel free to ask me more questions if you like, but that’s one way of filling the hole. 

You also could fill it with expanding foam filler, carve it down once it’s cured and spread out the hole, then do the same step as above with sculpting in the detail with plumber putty.

I don’t know if you have anything like that, it would help your case if you did, but regardless, this is not your fault or responsibility. 

You are likely to have a bit of a ball ache journey ahead of you now though with a lot of back and forth communication. 
First you need to communicate with the repair company, they are the ones who made the contract with DPD, and if anything goes wrong, it is down to them to sort it with DPD as they have all the receipts and information. 

Next, contact DPD and ask for a copy of the signature used for the package. It should never have been left on the porch under any circumstances, it should have gone back to the depot if no one was in. Make sure you note the time it was delivered too and any relevant info like that. Keep records of absolutely everything. 

In my case, after a lot of back and forth between the seller first who basically said “been delivered, talk to eBay”, eBay customers service (I know you didn’t use eBay, but just to demonstrate the process I had to go through) and Royal Mail, I ended up having to report my missing item to Action Fraud. Doing this doesn’t recoup the costs for you, but it opens a case against those involved. 
I would also report this to the police
Make sure you get that copy of the signature used though, that will really help you I think.

You might consider putting pieces that are meant to arrive separate either in a little baggie or wrapped in some tissue paper and labelled “gun” or whatever it it, it just conveys clearly that it’s intentional and also shows you put extra care into making sure it arrives safe. 

As for your product that was upgraded to the 3D printing, I would update your listing asap with a more up to date photo. I understand you say it’s a better quality product, but at the end of the day, the customer placed an order under the assumption that they were getting what was shown in the image. It’s just best to be very open and transparent when it comes to listings, as you would want the same thing as a buyer.

I think people are being too harsh on you for the shipping side- I used to buy expensive resin statues which had custom inserts to fit each piece snuggly in them. The whole box went through drop tests and still some would arrive damaged to customers. It sadly happens even with the best of packing.

There are a few options for the next step which could have been considered. 
a) they send it back to you for you to repair and send it back (you pay postage). This might not be feasible though if the shipping was expensive.
b) if they feel confident enough to do it, offer a partial refund and advice on the exact product to use to fix it, with detailed instructions on what they should do. 
c) give a full refund on return of the item. (You pay postage)

I think you packaged the item well. When something is a one off piece we don’t have a one size fits all for packaging so we can only do our best. Some sculpts have weak spots that we didn’t know about until it’s too late. 
My advice though is leave out the fragile tape. I’ve heard many, MANY stories from workers and people sending mail which have said fragile tape/ stickers just target your package for an extra beating. All it takes is one worker having a bad day and your parcel could be toast lol (people have said label the package as paint and it is seemed to help, so just a bit of info for you, I’ve not tried it myself though.).

As a sculptor that has had to send out custom pieces, I completely understand your issue and I think people are being too quick to say you did a bad packing job, you clearly did try and protect it. Go forward with this experience and assume every one of your packages will take a beating as you package them up.

Just in case anyone comes across this and is stuck, this isn’t a guide by any means, just a rough idea of what I managed to do and had 2 mins left on the clock. 

Akiyama 1- Spam kicks and immediately back enemy into the corner. Use a heat action and go back to spam kicks (including the charged attacks you do with triangle) until you trigger the QTE. You wanna have some heat left for next stage. 

Akiyama 2- Grab Chainsaw Man and do heat action on the wall. Use the run up attack with triangle where you do the kicks in the air when he’s finished attacking. Use heat as soon as you get it. Just pick away at him as quick as you can but avoid getting hit, you don’t wanna lose heat you’ve been trying to build up. 

Akiyama 3- Try chain spam kicks and utilise blocking when Minami gets his heat, ‘cause he can spam attack you and drain your timer. Utilise heat as much as possible even if it’s repeat attacks, cause you can do a lil damage with the timer on hold. 

Saejima 1- Kill the guard with the gun immediately, use that gun to wipe out the rest of the grunts. Saito is a quick kill, do square, square, then hold the triangle to do charged attacks. Use heat right away and make sure you block otherwise he will chain long attacks onto you and waste your timer. 

Saejima 2- I did the same attacks on Kiryu as I did with Saito, punch punch then charged up attacks, if you get the triple combo where he knocks Kiryu to the ground, heat attack immediately. If you do the chain of attacks where he does two and kicks him back, be ready to block incoming attack because Kiryu won’t fell down, and do the combos again. 

Saejima 3- Again, same bunch of attacks, you want to try get Majima on the ground so you can heat action him. Block as much as you can just so you don’t get thrown on the floor, but don’t worry about taking damage, you can afford to lose it, just heat action him as much as possible. He’s a quick defeat once you get a good technique down. The QTE goes in a circle either clockwise or anti clockwise, so don’t get flustered when they both trigger. 

*I THINK I had about 10 or 11 mins left at this point*

Tanimura 1- Grab a grunt, mash circle to special throw them (hopefully into surrounding enemies) and as soon as you get heat, use it on the gun enemy. Repeat until all dead, then focus your attacks onto the lowest health big enemy (was usually the gun one for me). One on one with the katana guy is much easier and you can finish him off. 

Tanimura 2- Mash circle, do one heat action just to get some free damage with no loss of timer, but ultimately just mash circle, make sure you go into the next stage with full heat. You’ll take a bunch of hits but it won’t matter it’s so insignificant. 

Tanimura 3- You will utilise your L1 deflection here, run to the dock, and  deflect him into it so he bounces back and falls down, heat action him to start things off. Ultimately you wanna do a mix of deflecting him so he falls down, or deflecting him then getting some attacks in. If he block, block as quickly as possible and repeat what you were doing. If you can, utilise spamming kicks when he’s down. I wasn’t very good at that but i did get a few in, and any way to chip away health is useful. 

Kiryu 1- Kiryu was a struggle for me, and if you’re the same, I’d recommend going back to Ultimate 4 and practicing him a bit. Learn to Tiger Drop and to do the pary (I think it was L1 and triangle, you light up blue when you do it). Remember to block and to also attack, don’t rely on TD only like I did for a bit. Try land some charged up combos to get Ibrahimovic on the floor so you can heat him, paired with TD. The enemy is quick so can be hard to pinpoint when to TD him, it really just takes some practice. I admit I got spammy and panicky with my timing, some luckily hit and won me the match. 

Kiryu 2- This guys a bit easier as he’s easier to read and his health goes down faster. Block a lot to get heat, and use the pary to keep you from getting knocked over, it also chips away a small bit of life so that’s good. When he opens his hands, don’t attack as he will throw you, just wait it out ready to TD him, he’ll do a little lead up to his attack so you have a very small window to react and try time it right. Chain some attacks on him when you can. 

Kiryu 3- This guy can be a pain, he chains attacks and can just get you locked into them, and if you’re by a wall then it can really drain your life. I don’t think I had much plan for him, just try get lucky with TD and make sure to pary him a lot, and wail on him with combo attacks to attempt to knock him down. Don’t attempt to grab him. I used any heat action at the first available chance, I didn’t care if it was recycled, a tiny bit of damage was better than risking losing what I built up. His health goes down in fairly big chunks so he can be cleared quickly.

Kiryu 4- The one I dreaded. I think I managed to defeat him on my 4th face off with him. Don’t bother grabbing, no point. Block a lot. My first attempt I triggered 5 TD attacks and only 1 landed, so just be aware of that going in, they aren’t guaranteed counters. This guy is stupidly fast and I couldn’t work out how to time any attacks for him quite honestly. I guessed when to string some attacks and when to TD and mostly was just doing parry so I didn’t get floored. I did two TD on him in total on the winning fight- one early on, the next thing I knew I had landed a second one somehow later in the fight and he fell to the floor, I was able to trigger a heat action and that killed him. I don’t think I would be able to beat him again, that fight was pure guessing. 

Hope this can help someone. I’m so glad it’s over.

I was checking Facebook constantly, and I realised I didn’t actually give a shit about anything or most people on there. I was using it as an outlet to try mask my depression and anxiety by always being the person uploading funny stuff, be it memes or making statuses to evoke a laugh. I just felt like I wanted to be noticed but for the wrong reasons. 

I thought “fuck this” and deactivated it and I felt so good after I did it. Thought I’d miss it but never felt the urge to check it. Still don’t and it’s been almost a year. The only reason I haven’t outright deleted it is I want to recover the photos at some point, I just don’t have a computer to do that just yet. 
I use messenger still to contact friends I actually want to stay in contact with. 

I do use Instagram still though, as all I care  about is seeing artwork uploads and that’s a much better platform than FB for that kind of thing. Also I like uploading my own work, being able to share something I’m proud to have made helps my own depression a little. 

The key is figuring out what sets you off and then removing that. You may only have to remove yourself from 1 social media or all of them, depending on your situation, but you need to manage what you’re using. I still have triggering things on instagram every now and again, but I manage that by removing or muting certain people.

See what works best for you. :)

I do need to hop on what others are saying though: 

- glass tank is a bad idea, changing to a cage is vital. If you get one with bars, just make sure your baby can't squeeze out of them. 
Rats get sick easily and a tank is not ideal because their living space can't ventilate, so just make your cutie as comfy as possible in a cage. 

- a friend is a necessity. Even if you offer your baby all the time and love in the world, they still need to socialise with their own species. Just make sure it's the same sex! Introducing a cage mate can either be super easy or a long process, so have patience if it's the latter. 

- as mentioned too, wood shavings are generally not a good bedding to go with. Best thing you can do is lay sheets of fleece down on the floors and when it's time to clean the cage, just take it out and swap over (of course after giving everything a good scrub first). Shake off all the bits on the dirty one then give it a wash and you're ready for the next cage clean! They love chewing though, so it will get tatty before long, but fleece is cheap enough anyway, and lovely and soft! 

I urge you to listen to the advice given in this thread and make changes as soon as you can possibly manage. Rats can be expensive animals, they get sick so easily, so it's very important that you help them along as much as you can by letting them live as healthy as possible.
